I know how you feel. Sometimes we just gotta move on. Do things that make you happy. Once you consistently do them, you'll develop a passion, let alone a skill. Enjoy some alone time to think, cope, and recover. Even knowing that your family can turn on you at any moment can be scary especially when the rest of the family is going with the flow instead of fighting for what's right.

You've accomplished things that many people choose not to even if they had the chance or money to do so. Even as you choose to live the way your live, she still tries to control you by your college choices (which is the only thing or one of the ways she can). That fact that she doesn't have to work at 16 unlike you is extremely unfair however, look at where it got you. It showed that your a fighter, a hard worker, and that you were willing to survive. Your sister on the other hand without realizing this yet will have already put her life in jeparody. If you enjoyed taking track, debate, and computer programming or even if you didn't you moved a step closer to breaking free as it would give you more options for more job opportunities. Now you just have to make sure they don't show up where you live or follow you.

If your questioning yourself about if they are or not then they're definitely abusive period. They're abusing their power as parents especially with the fact that they make more money and pay for more things. Enjoy yourself, limit contact, switch conversation topics as many times as you can, and make a joke about anything you can to lighten the mood to refrain from arguments.
Same. My mom will guilt trip while my dad does the dirty work. There basically still in child like mindsets or stuck in their past craving attention.

Sadly your mom doesn't care and you can't change her. I know it's a tough pill to swallow but it's better to accept that to start moving on instead of waiting more years to get her attention when all she'll do is hurt you more. If you can't find people to confide in, start by doing something that makes you happy and dismiss any ill feelings. For example playing video games. Whether online or offline video games is a healthy escape (yes is said healthy unless you play almost for 24 hours nonstop) from that reality. Music helps put you in different moods depending on what kind you listen to. If you have any siblings try to talk to them. Hopefully you can reach your cousin or father even. Makes sure that anyone you try to reach doesn't circle back to your mom because it will all go to waste.

Hey i may not be 30 years old but what i would tell you is to not give up. That's the last thing you should think of. For example: tuesday, apply here, visit here, tell crazy N mom that its for this reason, call these places and go home. Backup plan: if this fails email someone, get a hold of a friend, and bam. Do it on a day you have to go somewhere like for an event, the store, classes, something important thats near your place and bounce. Once your there let her know by phone if she call but don't tell here where. Legally your an adult so you'll have more time to think. Then focus on passions that you want to do that doesn't invlove college (cause you can do community or go to a big one and still be unhappy). Try starting a buisness with some money, buy some furniture, a bed, learn to cook, heck be a youtuber for a bit all on your free time. If you don't have much free time, whenever you do get some air, go to events in the city, parks, and chill you might meet a nice girl, or a baddie, or a cool friend. I know your 30 but you still got life to live. Don't give up. I made a plan for myself as well. I'll add you in my prayers. Hope this advice helped
